acquisition: Data were acquired using the Q-Exactive Plus mass spectrometer in data-dependent MS/MS mode.

Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics
workflow_hints: By amber-codon suppression we map the Mis18-binding sites for the R1 and R2 repeat by mass spectrometry
unnatural amino-acids with photo-activatable cross-linker groups, p-benzoyl-L-phenylalanine (Bpa) and 3′-azibutyl-N-carbamoyl-lysine (AbK)
Program StavroX version 3.6.6.6 was used for cross-link identification.

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses photo-cross-linking via genetic code expansion (amber suppression) to incorporate unnatural amino acids (Bpa and AbK) to map protein-protein interactions. This is a specialized complexome/structural proteomics workflow. While 'LFQ' is not explicitly mentioned, the DDA acquisition and lack of isobaric tags suggest a label-free approach for identification of cross-linked peptides.

scope: HJURP proteins with incorporated Bpa or AbK were incubated with Mis18α: Mis18β complex and cross-linked by UV light.
Cross-linked products were further purified using Ni2+ affinity resin, washed with urea buffer, and subjected to proteolysis and mass spectrometry (MS) analysis.
The protein solutions were incubated with 10¹L Ni resin (Roche), and MBP-HJURP variants carrying 8His-tags at the C-termini bound on Ni resin together with Mis18α56–C:Mis18β.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on purified recombinant protein complexes (HJURP and Mis18α/β) captured via Ni-affinity resin following UV cross-linking.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment is a chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) study. The primary biological variable is the genetic modification (incorporation of unnatural amino acids and point mutations) used to map protein-protein interaction interfaces. The UV light is a technical trigger for the cross-linking assay rather than a biological perturbation of a living system.
